thesis: Mohnish Pabrai argues that India's disappointing sports performance compared to nations like Jamaica can be improved by adopting a specialized system where world-class coaches identify potential children at ages 10 to 12, gather them into a centralized environment, and provide years of professional coaching before they reach high school. He illustrates that this deep interest and specialization, driven by peer influence and role models, is the reason small countries dominate specific sports like sprinting, baseball, and soccer despite having smaller populations than larger nations like the United States.
